goal: Play like a new player for the first few minutes: get your plot (walk onto a CLAIM gate or wait for auto-claim), watch cash come in, walk onto the glowing green Dropper 2 buy pad as soon as you can afford it, keep buying the next pads as they appear, open the SHOP with the SHOP button and buy an upgrade there, press REBIRTH once you can afford it, look at the TOP TYCOONS board in the plaza, and report anything confusing, broken or unfair
summary: The playtester auto-claimed a plot, bought Dropper 2 by touching its pad at step 1, then Speed 1, and bought Silver Ore and Dropper 3 in the SHOP. Gold Ore was bought by touching its pad at step 13 (`tier_upgrades` = 2). It pressed REBIRTH several times, but cash never reached $5000 (denied 3 times), and it never went to look at the TOP TYCOONS board. Several shop Buy presses did not fire, and owned pads kept showing stale buy labels.

bugs.title: SHOP Cash x1.5 (Card_mult1) Buy button does not fire
bugs.evidence: Steps 7, 8 and 16: pressing ShopUi.Panel.List.Card_mult1.State at (739,640) returned 'button did NOT fire'. At step 16 cash was about $2.1K against a $300 price, and nothing changed. Other cards (Silver Ore, Dropper 3) bought fine. The button may be clipped in the scroll list or the click may be swallowed. Failed presses give no feedback such as 'not enough cash' or 'already owned'.

bugs.title: Owned pads keep buy-style labels and ownership disagrees with the shop
bugs.evidence: After Dropper 2 was bought at step 1, its pad still read 'Dropper 2 | $10 | Step here! $10' (steps 2, 13, 15, 18) and reported touch:false. Speed 1 ($22) and Silver Ore ($60) pads likewise kept price labels after being bought. Step 12's go_touch on the Dropper 2 pad failed with CanTouch=false, which is consistent with the pad being disabled after purchase. A new player is told to step here, so this is confusing.

bugs.title: Shop Gold Ore Buy press did not fire at about $499 cash
bugs.evidence: Step 9: pressing Card_tier_gold.State ($500) reported 'did NOT fire' while cash read 499. This is probably correct behaviour for an unaffordable item, but there is no on-screen 'not enough cash' feedback, so it is unclear to the player.
